History_of_Present_Illness.content: Suprapubic/lower midline abdominal pain rated 7/10, intermittent
No lower back or loin pain
No prior similar episodes or urinary tract infections
No recent exercise, dehydration, or increased sexual activity

Medications.content: Three-day course of antibiotics prescribed for suspected LUTI (drug not specified)
Continue mebeverine 200 mg three times daily for IBS

Family_History.content: No known family history issues reported

Social_and_Family_History.content: Alcohol intake approximately one glass of wine per week

Assessment.content: Suspected uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (LUTI)
LUTI supported by 6 days of dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, and hematuria
Assessment.source_text: 6 days dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, hematuria

Assessment.content: LUTI assessment notes patient is afebrile, has no flank or loin pain, and is able to void
Assessment.source_text: afebrile; no flank/loin pain; able to void

Assessment.content: IBS assessment notes no change in bowel habit and no weight loss
Assessment.source_text: no change in bowel habit; no weight loss

Plan_of_Care.content: Three-day course of antibiotics prescribed for suspected LUTI
Antibiotic prescription sent electronically to Knightsbridge Practice pharmacy
Patient to pick up antibiotics in approximately one hour
Advise hydration of 2.5–3 liters per day
Consider cranberry juice for symptom management
Recommend over-the-counter urinary alkalinizing sachets; details to be added to notes
Plan_of_Care.source_text: OTC urinary alkalinizing sachets; details to be added to notes

Plan_of_Care.content: Obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature
No routine urine test needed unless symptoms worsen or are not resolving
Plan_of_Care.source_text: No routine urine test needed unless symptoms worsen/not resolving

Plan_of_Care.content: No need to call after completing antibiotics if fully better
Plan_of_Care.source_text: No need to call after completing antibiotics if fully better

Plan_of_Care.content: For IBS, continue mebeverine 200 mg three times daily

Follow_up_Information.content: Seek review if worsening pain, new lower back or loin pain, fever, difficulty passing urine, or recurrent symptoms
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Safety-net: seek review if worsening pain, new lower back/loin pain, fever, difficulty passing urine, or recurrent symptoms
